Product accumulation and long-term depletion are excluded, making the target an instantaneous catalytic rate controlled by competition for enzyme occupancy.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.k_cat: positive assay-dependent range spanning materially different catalytic environments while preserving active enzyme and initial-rate conditions

derivation_notes: The binding competition law is retained, but the previous dataset-wide constant k_cat is reinterpreted as an externally controlled assay condition that can vary between measurements, representing environment-dependent turnover of the enzyme-substrate complex. This changes the scored mapping because v_instantaneous now legitimately varies across matched S, I, and E_total when k_cat differs between assays.
change_summary: The assumption of one fixed catalytic turnover number for the whole dataset is relaxed by promoting k_cat to an independently varied input. The resulting rate law keeps competitive occupancy unchanged while adding observable environment-dependent modulation of the catalytic rate scale.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: All enzyme molecules have the same catalytic capacity, represented as a single constant k_cat shared by every measurement.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Condition-dependent catalytic turnover, such as temperature- or medium-dependent changes in the chemistry of the substrate-bound catalytic step, while competitive binding remains the same first approximation.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Recover the parent law when k_cat is held fixed across all experiments, so the promoted condition no longer varies between measurements.

response_change.parent_relation: With fixed k_cat, the rate depends on S and I only through competitive occupancy: for any fixed E_total the normalized surface v_instantaneous/E_total is a Michaelis-Menten function of S with inhibitor effect entering only as the linear factor 1 + I/K_i in the apparent denominator.
response_change.child_relation: Release k_cat from being constant and allow catalytic turnover to depend on an experimental condition such as temperature, so the target becomes jointly shaped by occupancy and environment-dependent turnover. Then at the same S, I, and E_total, the rate changes with the added condition, and the relative inhibitor effect can differ across that condition because occupancy and turnover scales interact in the full response surface.
response_change.observable_effect: Across assays performed at different values of the promoted condition, the maximal rate scale changes even when substrate and inhibitor concentrations are held fixed; one shared parent parameter set cannot match those condition-dependent rate shifts because the parent has no channel for that variation except a single global k_cat.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The model assumes one fixed catalytic turnover number across all measurements, omitting experimentally admissible variation in catalytic capacity between assay conditions.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: All enzyme molecules have the same catalytic capacity, represented as a single constant k_cat shared by every measurement.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Condition-dependent catalytic turnover, such as temperature- or medium-dependent changes in the chemistry of the substrate-bound catalytic step, while competitive binding remains the same first approximation.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the assumption that k_cat is one fixed constant for the entire dataset. The parent target mapping has a fixed-environment shortcut: once S, I, and E_total are specified, all assay-to-assay differences must be absorbed by one shared turnover constant. Under a scientifically admissible design where the catalytic environment varies across measurements but initial-rate conditions still hold, one can compare rates at fixed S, I, and E_total while changing the promoted condition controlling k_cat. The parent predicts no change except through a single global refit, whereas the child allows a systematic additional dependence of the measured target itself. This is a genuine target-mapping change, not merely an auxiliary trajectory change, because v_instantaneous is the scored output and it varies directly with the promoted condition. The effect is observable when the environment changes turnover appreciably but leaves the enzyme active and the competitive-binding picture still approximately valid. A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce distinct rate levels across those conditions because it lacks any input channel for them; separate fits per condition would violate the shared-parameter requirement. The scientific continuation path is clear: if all assays are run at one fixed environment, or if turnover variation is negligible, the child collapses back to the parent.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.inhibitor_nonlinearity: nonnegative dimensionless range from near 0 up to order-1 values where deviation from linear competitive inhibition becomes experimentally visible without leaving reversible initial-rate conditions

derivation_notes: The parent assumes the competitive inhibition factor is exactly linear in inhibitor load, 1 + I/K_i. Relaxing ideal dilute inhibitor competition gives an apparent substrate competition factor that includes a quadratic correction in the dimensionless inhibitor occupancy pressure, yielding a stronger right-shift of the substrate response at high I while preserving the same initial-rate occupancy framework.
change_summary: The inhibitor penalty in the Michaelis denominator was refined from a strictly linear function of I/K_i to a nonlinear one with a quadratic crowding/non-ideality term. This changes the scored mapping itself by introducing stronger curvature in rate suppression versus inhibitor concentration, especially when I/K_i is not small.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Reversible competitive inhibition remains ideal and linear in inhibitor concentration across the full assay range, so the apparent half-saturation scale is exactly K_m*(1 + I/K_i).
assumption_audit.mechanism: Non-ideal competitive inhibition or crowding/activity effects in inhibitor binding make inhibitor occupancy pressure increase the apparent substrate competition more than linearly at higher inhibitor exposure.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed E_total and I, v_instantaneous increases hyperbolically with S, with inhibition entering only as a linear multiplier of K_m through 1 + I/K_i.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the ideal competitive-binding term with an inhibitor effect that changes the apparent substrate competition nonlinearly at higher I, so the S-response and inhibitor-response bend more strongly than the parent's single linear occupancy penalty.
response_change.observable_effect: When E_total is held fixed and rates are measured across increasing I, the child predicts stronger-than-linear growth of the apparent half-saturation substrate scale versus I, causing extra downward curvature in v versus I and stronger right-shift of v versus S at high inhibitor levels than the parent can match with one shared parameter set.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Visible when inhibitor spans from weak to substantial competition, with I/K_i not confined to the asymptotically small regime, while S is sampled around and below the inhibited half-saturation range so curvature changes are not masked by full substrate saturation.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate inhibitor already alters the local slope of v versus S; in holdout, extending to higher I reveals that the apparent K_m shift grows nonlinearly rather than remaining proportional to I, preserving the same mechanism across both regions.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent in the limit where the added nonlinearity in inhibitor competition tends to zero, so the apparent competition factor returns to 1 + I/K_i.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Non-ideal competitive inhibition or crowding/activity effects in inhibitor binding make the inhibitor-induced increase in apparent substrate competition deviate from the simple linear law at higher inhibitor exposure.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than coefficient-only correction because the inhibitor and dissociation scale are first combined into the dimensionless load I/K_i and then passed through a nonlinear map that changes the denominator curvature, altering how S and I jointly control the measured rate.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The current model assumes ideal dilute competitive inhibition, where inhibitor increases the substrate half-saturation scale strictly linearly in I/K_i across all admissible inhibitor levels.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Competitive inhibitor occupancy remains reversible but becomes non-ideal at higher inhibitor exposure, so the apparent half-saturation shift is a nonlinear function of I/K_i.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Setting inhibitor_nonlinearity = 0 recovers the parent exactly.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Parent response relationship: with E_total fixed, increasing I shifts the substrate curve through the affine scale K_m*(1 + I/K_i), so the inhibited transition point grows linearly with I. Child change: the denominator uses K_m*(1 + I/K_i + inhibitor_nonlinearity*(I/K_i)**2), so the apparent half-saturation scale bends upward with I and the rate-versus-I suppression gains extra curvature. This changed target mapping is observable when I/K_i reaches moderate values and S is measured near or below the inhibited transition region; under those conditions the child shows a stronger high-I right-shift of v versus S and stronger downward curvature of v versus I than the parent.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set can only produce an apparent half-saturation scale affine in I, because all inhibitor dependence enters through 1 + I/K_i. Refitting K_m and K_i can change the slope and intercept of that affine relation but cannot reproduce both the low-I behavior and the stronger high-I bending implied by a quadratic inhibitor-load correction across the same shared dataset. This is a change in the scored rate mapping itself, not merely in an auxiliary trajectory.

evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Relax the assumption that reversible inhibitor competition remains ideal and linear in inhibitor concentration over the whole assay range.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Non-ideal competitive inhibition or crowding/activity effects in inhibitor binding make the inhibitor-induced increase in apparent substrate competition deviate from the simple linear law at higher inhibitor exposure.
evolution_plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: with E_total and k_cat fixed, v is Michaelis-Menten in S and the inhibitor acts only by a single linear shift of the denominator through I/K_i. A realistic next refinement is to keep the same instantaneous competitive-occupancy picture but relax the ideal linear inhibitor term. Distinguishing condition: vary I over a materially broad range while also sampling S near the inhibited transition region, holding E_total fixed. Then the parent predicts that the apparent half-saturation scale K_m*(1 + I/K_i) is affine in I, so all inhibition curves are tied to one linear occupancy penalty. The child predicts a changed target mapping: the slope and curvature of v with respect to I and S change because the inhibitor penalty grows nonlinearly at higher I. This is observable in the scored rate itself, not merely in an auxiliary quantity. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce both low-I behavior and the stronger high-I right-shift/downward curvature if the true apparent K_m-versus-I relation is non-affine. The refinement is admissible under initial-rate conditions, requires no new variable, and vanishes back to the parent in the weak-nonlinearity limit. Limitation: if all data remain at I/K_i much less than 1 or at S far above all inhibited half-saturation scales, the distinction may be weak.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.substrate_self_inhibition: nonnegative dimensionless range from near 0 up to order-1 values, with clearly observable effects when S is comparable to or exceeds K_m but still within reversible initial-rate conditions

derivation_notes: The parent assumes substrate contributes ideally as a single linear S term in the denominator. Relaxing that assumption, weak substrate self-inhibition or substrate-induced crowding is represented as an additional high-S loss term proportional to S**2/K_m that competes with productive saturation without introducing new measured variables.
change_summary: Added a substrate-load-dependent competing penalty in the denominator to capture weak high-substrate flattening of the initial-rate curve. This preserves competitive inhibition by I while changing the substrate-response curvature at fixed I and E_total.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The substrate contribution to the initial-rate law remains ideal Michaelis-Menten at all admissible substrate concentrations, with no substrate-side self-crowding or self-inhibition.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Weak substrate self-inhibition or substrate-induced crowding of productive enzyme occupancy adds a competing high-substrate loss process within the initial-rate regime.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when substrate_self_inhibition -> 0.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed E_total and I, v_instantaneous increases hyperbolically with S using a single inhibitor-independent K_m term modified only by inhibitor occupancy, so the normalized substrate-response shape is the same apart from the competitive right-shift in apparent affinity.
response_change.child_relation: Retain competitive inhibition but relax the assumption that substrate binding remains ideal at all substrate loads by allowing weak substrate self-crowding/self-inhibition in the substrate-dependent denominator contribution, so the rate bends downward relative to the parent at high S even when I is fixed.
response_change.observable_effect: When I and E_total are held fixed and S is swept into a regime comparable to or above K_m, the child predicts a weaker approach to saturation than the parent; across low-S and high-S portions of the same sweep, one shared parent parameter set cannot match both the initial rise and the extra high-S flattening.

evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Weak substrate self-inhibition or substrate-induced crowding of productive enzyme binding causes the effective substrate-response curve to flatten at high substrate concentration even before leaving the initial-rate regime.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it inserts a new substrate-dependent competing process with distinct scaling in S, changing curvature across a single substrate sweep rather than simply shifting gain or apparent affinity.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Substrate binding/turnover remains perfectly ideal on the substrate side over the whole initial-rate sweep, so substrate enters the denominator only through a single linear S term.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: At high substrate load, productive catalysis competes with weak substrate self-crowding/self-inhibition, adding a nonlinear substrate penalty while retaining reversible competitive inhibition by I.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The child collapses exactly to the parent when substrate_self_inhibition = 0.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: At fixed I and E_total, low-S behavior remains close to the parent, but once S reaches order K_m or higher the added S**2/K_m penalty produces extra downward curvature and slower saturation. This changes the scored mapping v(S,I,E_total) itself: the parent gives one hyperbolic substrate-response family after inhibitor-dependent right-shift, whereas the child yields stronger high-S flattening under the same fixed inhibitor condition.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent parameters cannot generally absorb this effect across low-S and high-S regions because changing k_cat only rescales the whole curve and changing K_m or K_i only repositions the hyperbola through an apparent affinity shift. None of those parent parameters creates the new high-S quadratic denominator growth, so one shared parent parameter set cannot match both the initial rise and the stronger late flattening under fixed I and E_total.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the substrate contribution to the rate law stays ideal Michaelis-Menten at all admissible substrate concentrations, with non-ideality allowed only on the inhibitor side.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Relax the assumption that substrate binding/turnover remains perfectly first-order in the denominator contribution with respect to substrate load over the whole initial-rate sweep.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Weak substrate self-inhibition or substrate-induced crowding of productive enzyme binding causes the effective substrate-response curve to flatten at high substrate concentration even before leaving the initial-rate regime.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to modify the substrate-side idealization rather than adding a new species. The parent already captures reversible competitive inhibition and a nonlinear inhibitor occupancy penalty, but at fixed I and E_total it still enforces a single Michaelis-type substrate saturation shape. In many enzyme assays, sufficiently high substrate can weakly reduce productive turnover or productive binding through self-inhibition/crowding without requiring product buildup or time dependence. The distinguishing condition is a substrate sweep with I held fixed at low or moderate reversible values and E_total held fixed: the parent predicts a standard hyperbolic rise whose curvature is fully determined by one apparent affinity term, whereas the child predicts additional downward curvature at higher S. This changes the scored mapping v(S,I,E_total), not merely an auxiliary trajectory. The effect is admissible only when S reaches order K_m or above; if all data remain far below K_m, the refinement would be poorly identifiable, which is a limitation.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Introduce a gain or loss that competes with an existing process in different state regions.

scenario_text: A catalytic enzyme converts substrate while a reversible inhibitor competes for access to the same free enzyme population. Initial reaction rates are measured independently at varied substrate, inhibitor, and enzyme concentrations. Product accumulation and long-term depletion are excluded, making the target an instantaneous catalytic rate controlled by competition for enzyme occupancy.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed E_total and I, v_instantaneous increases hyperbolically with S using a single inhibitor-independent K_m term modified only by inhibitor occupancy, so the normalized substrate-response shape is the same apart from the competitive right-shift in apparent affinity.
response_change.child_relation: Retain competitive inhibition but relax the assumption that substrate binding remains ideal at all substrate loads by allowing weak substrate self-crowding/self-inhibition in the substrate-dependent denominator contribution, so the rate bends downward relative to the parent at high S even when I is fixed.
response_change.observable_effect: When I and E_total are held fixed and S is swept into a regime comparable to or above K_m, the child predicts a weaker approach to saturation than the parent; across low-S and high-S portions of the same sweep, one shared parent parameter set cannot match both the initial rise and the extra high-S flattening.

activation_condition: Observable when substrate is varied from sub-K_m to several-fold K_m while inhibitor remains in a reversible initial-rate regime; the refinement is most visible at moderate-to-high substrate load where ideal Michaelis saturation begins to fail but finite initial-rate assumptions still hold.
train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate S already shows slight downward deviation from the parent's simple hyperbola; in holdout at higher S with similar I and E_total, the same mechanism produces stronger flattening rather than a mere rescaling.
continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit of vanishing substrate self-crowding/self-inhibition strength.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.crowding_inhibitor_coupling: nonnegative dimensionless range from near 0 up to order-1 or few, with observable effects when both I/K_i and S/K_m are at least order 1

derivation_notes: The parent law assumes the substrate self-inhibition coefficient is independent of inhibitor load. Here that coefficient is refined to substrate_self_inhibition*(1 + crowding_inhibitor_coupling*I/K_i)**2, representing mixed active-site occupancy/crowding where inhibitor presence exacerbates the high-substrate penalty while preserving the parent in the zero-coupling limit.
change_summary: Changed the assumption that substrate self-crowding is separable from inhibitor competition. The successor introduces an inhibitor-dependent strengthening of the high-substrate penalty, creating an observable S-by-I interaction in the initial-rate mapping.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The coefficient of the high-substrate penalty substrate_self_inhibition*S**2/K_m is constant across inhibitor conditions.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Mixed occupancy/crowding at the enzyme active-site environment: inhibitor binding or near-site occupancy can exacerbate the loss of productive turnover caused by high substrate loading, producing an S-by-I interaction in the high-substrate regime.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Set crowding_inhibitor_coupling = 0 to recover the parent expression exactly.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed E_total and k_cat, inhibitor only increases the apparent competition term through a substrate-independent factor 1 + I/K_i + inhibitor_nonlinearity*(I/K_i)**2, so the shape of the S-response under inhibition differs mainly by a single horizontal penalty plus the existing substrate self-inhibition term.
response_change.child_relation: Make the high-substrate self-inhibition/crowding strength itself increase with inhibitor load, so inhibitor not only shifts the low-S apparent affinity but also strengthens the high-S downturn/flattening of the S-response.
response_change.observable_effect: When comparing rate-versus-substrate curves at low versus moderate/high inhibitor with E_total and k_cat held fixed, the child predicts a stronger suppression near S comparable to or above K_m than expected from a shared pure competitive shift, i.e. inhibition becomes disproportionately larger in the high-S regime.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when both S/K_m is at least order 1 and I/K_i is at least order 1, so that substrate self-crowding is already relevant and inhibitor occupancy is non-negligible; weak or absent when either S << K_m or I << K_i.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, moderate inhibitor already changes the curvature of v versus S beyond a simple right-shift; in holdout, higher joint S and I extends this into a clearer high-S suppression pattern rather than merely stronger low-S competition.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit of zero inhibitor dependence of the substrate self-inhibition strength, so the substrate_self_inhibition term becomes independent of I.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: inhibitor-amplified substrate crowding in the active-site environment
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Mixed occupancy/crowding at the enzyme active-site environment: inhibitor binding or near-site occupancy can exacerbate the loss of productive turnover caused by high substrate loading, producing an S-by-I interaction in the high-substrate regime.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the inhibitor load first modulates the self-inhibition strength and that combined quantity is then applied inside the nonlinear denominator term multiplying S**2/K_m, changing curvature of v(S) across inhibitor conditions rather than just rescaling one global slope or affinity term.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The high-substrate penalty and inhibitor competition act as separable effects on the rate law, with a constant substrate_self_inhibition coefficient.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Inhibitor occupancy strengthens the effective substrate self-inhibition coefficient, creating a mixed S-by-I crowding interaction in the denominator.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Set crowding_inhibitor_coupling = 0 to recover the parent exactly.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: At fixed E_total and k_cat, compare v versus S across low and moderate/high I. The parent permits inhibitor-dependent low-S suppression but keeps the onset and strength of the high-S flattening/downturn tied to one inhibitor-independent substrate_self_inhibition term, whereas the child adds extra high-S suppression that grows with I when S/K_m and I/K_i are both order 1 or larger.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent parameters cannot create inhibitor-specific changes in the high-S curvature without simultaneously changing the same substrate_self_inhibition term for all inhibitor conditions. Retuning K_m, K_i, or inhibitor_nonlinearity only alters the competitive penalty structure, and retuning substrate_self_inhibition changes all I curves together, so one shared parent parameter set cannot reproduce disproportionately stronger inhibition only in the joint high-S, high-I regime.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model treats substrate self-inhibition as independent of inhibitor load, implicitly assuming that the high-substrate penalty and inhibitor competition act as separable effects on the rate law.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The coefficient of the high-substrate penalty substrate_self_inhibition*S**2/K_m is constant across inhibitor conditions.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Mixed occupancy/crowding at the enzyme active-site environment: inhibitor binding or near-site occupancy can exacerbate the loss of productive turnover caused by high substrate loading, producing an S-by-I interaction in the high-substrate regime.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the separability between competitive inhibition and substrate self-crowding. In the parent, varying I at fixed E_total and k_cat mainly changes the apparent competitive denominator at all S, while the high-S penalty set by substrate_self_inhibition is unchanged; thus one shared parameter set can only produce an inhibitor-independent onset and strength of the high-S flattening/downturn. The proposed child instead allows inhibitor presence to strengthen that high-S penalty, creating a true S-I interaction in the scored mapping v(S,I,E_total). The concrete distinguishing condition is to compare v versus S at two inhibitor levels while holding E_total and k_cat fixed: at low I the curve shows the parent-like mild high-S flattening, whereas at moderate/high I and S comparable to or above K_m the child predicts extra suppression beyond a competitive right-shift. This effect is scientifically admissible in initial-rate conditions as a phenomenological crowding/occupancy interaction and remains finite and rate-vanishing at S=0 or E_total=0. Limitation: if experiments only probe S well below K_m or I well below K_i, the contrast is weak and the parent may suffice.

expression: k_cat*E_total*S/(K_m*(1 + I/K_i + inhibitor_nonlinearity*(I/K_i)**2) + S + substrate_self_inhibition*(1 + crowding_inhibitor_coupling*(I/K_i)/(1 + I/K_i))**2*S**2/K_m)

Dimensionless coefficient capturing non-ideal nonlinear strengthening of inhibitor competition at higher inhibitor load
Dimensionless coefficient for weak substrate self-crowding or self-inhibition that adds a high-substrate penalty to productive turnover

derivation_notes: The competitive inhibition branch is retained, but the inhibitor modulation of the high-substrate self-inhibition branch is re-derived as an occupancy-limited effect using (I/K_i)/(1 + I/K_i), which approaches a finite ceiling as inhibitor binding becomes prevalent. This preserves the parent law to first order at low I/K_i while changing the high-S curvature of the S-by-I interaction.
change_summary: Changed the assumption that inhibitor-amplified substrate self-crowding grows indefinitely with I/K_i. The successor makes that amplification saturate with inhibitor occupancy, producing a bounded high-S interaction while leaving low-S competitive inhibition essentially unchanged.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The parent treats inhibitor enhancement of the high-substrate self-inhibition branch as indefinitely increasing with inhibitor concentration through a fixed polynomial factor (1 + crowding_inhibitor_coupling*I/K_i)^2.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Finite-site occupancy near the active-site environment causes inhibitor-dependent amplification of substrate self-crowding to saturate once most enzyme molecules are already affected, rather than strengthening without bound.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed E_total and I, the rate rises with S and then is suppressed only by a quadratic high-substrate crowding term whose inhibitor coupling is itself purely polynomial, so inhibitor action across S remains a single-phase strengthening of apparent competition/self-crowding.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the assumption that inhibitor-induced amplification of substrate self-inhibition grows indefinitely with I/K_i; instead let that amplification approach a finite occupancy-controlled ceiling, changing how the high-S penalty curves with I while preserving competitive inhibition at low S.
response_change.observable_effect: At high S, increasing I initially steepens the decline in v_instantaneous more strongly, but beyond I/K_i of order 1 the extra inhibitor-induced self-crowding effect bends toward saturation rather than continuing to grow quadratically with I; the parent cannot match both the early strengthening and the later flattening with one shared parameter set.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when sigma is order 1 or larger so the S**2/K_m penalty matters, and iota spans from small to order 1 or a few so inhibitor occupancy moves from weak to substantial; at low S the refinement is effectively hidden because the self-inhibition branch is negligible.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training-like moderate inhibitor ranges the child can resemble the parent, but when high-S measurements include both moderate and larger I, the child predicts diminishing incremental inhibitor-induced worsening whereas the parent keeps increasing the same interaction branch too strongly.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the inhibitor modulation of substrate self-inhibition is weak over the sampled range, e.g. crowding_inhibitor_coupling near 0 or I/K_i much less than 1 so the saturating and polynomial forms coincide to first order.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: occupancy-limited modulation of substrate self-crowding by inhibitor binding
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Finite-site occupancy near the active-site environment causes inhibitor-dependent amplification of substrate self-crowding to saturate once most enzyme molecules are already affected, rather than strengthening without bound.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because it changes the I-dependent curvature of an existing S-coupled penalty branch: the modulation now matches low-I onset but bends toward a ceiling at larger occupancy, which cannot be reproduced by merely rescaling the parent polynomial factor.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The parent treats inhibitor enhancement of the high-substrate self-inhibition branch as indefinitely increasing with inhibitor concentration through a fixed polynomial factor (1 + crowding_inhibitor_coupling*I/K_i)^2.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Inhibitor amplification of the substrate self-inhibition branch is occupancy-limited and saturates as inhibitor binding approaches a finite active-site-environment ceiling.
evolution_contract.after_fragment: k_cat*E_total*S/(K_m*(1 + I/K_i + inhibitor_nonlinearity*(I/K_i)**2) + S + substrate_self_inhibition*(1 + crowding_inhibitor_coupling*(I/K_i)/(1 + I/K_i))**2*S**2/K_m)
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: For I/K_i much less than 1, (I/K_i)/(1 + I/K_i) = I/K_i + higher-order terms, so the child recovers the parent interaction to first order; similarly, when crowding_inhibitor_coupling is near 0 the distinction is negligible.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: At fixed E_total and high substrate loading S/K_m of order 1 or larger, scan inhibitor concentration from low to moderate/high I/K_i: low-I behavior remains close to the parent, but the inhibitor-induced increase in the high-S penalty progressively flattens because the modulation factor (1 + crowding_inhibitor_coupling*(I/K_i)/(1 + I/K_i))**2 approaches a ceiling. This changes the scored mapping v_instantaneous(S,I,E_total), not an auxiliary trajectory, and is most visible where substrate_self_inhibition*S**2/K_m materially contributes to the denominator.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both the near-onset behavior at modest I/K_i and the later occupancy-limited flattening at larger I/K_i while preserving the same low-S competitive branch, because its only S-by-I self-crowding interaction uses the unbounded polynomial factor (1 + crowding_inhibitor_coupling*I/K_i)**2 with fixed curvature. Retuning substrate_self_inhibition or crowding_inhibitor_coupling changes overall strength but does not create saturation of the incremental inhibitor effect on the high-S branch.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the inhibitor-amplified substrate self-crowding factor grows as an unbounded polynomial in I/K_i, even though occupancy-mediated local crowding near a finite enzyme population should approach a ceiling as inhibitor binding becomes prevalent.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The parent treats inhibitor enhancement of the high-substrate self-inhibition branch as indefinitely increasing with inhibitor concentration through a fixed polynomial factor (1 + crowding_inhibitor_coupling*I/K_i)^2.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Finite-site occupancy near the active-site environment causes inhibitor-dependent amplification of substrate self-crowding to saturate once most enzyme molecules are already affected, rather than strengthening without bound.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to change the mathematical form of the existing S-by-I self-crowding interaction, not to add a new process. The parent already includes inhibitor-coupled substrate self-inhibition, but it assumes one single-phase polynomial growth with I. Vary I at fixed E_total and high S comparable to or above K_m, and compare rates across low-to-moderate versus moderate-to-high I/K_i. In the parent, the inhibitor-dependent worsening of the high-S penalty keeps accelerating according to the same polynomial branch. In the refined child, the same interaction emerges at low I but then bends toward a ceiling because only a finite fraction of enzyme active-site environments can be perturbed. This changes the scored mapping v_instantaneous(S,I,E_total), not merely an auxiliary trajectory. The contrast is scientifically admissible only when substrate self-inhibition is already active; if S is small relative to K_m, both parent and child reduce to nearly the same competitive-inhibition law and the refinement is not observable. A single refit of the parent cannot simultaneously capture near-linear onset in I at modest occupancy and reduced incremental effect at larger occupancy while preserving the same low-I behavior, because its interaction branch has fixed polynomial curvature with no saturation scale beyond the existing linear occupancy ratio.
